milestone: M56 Arbitrary Repository Coding Golden Journey

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: headless.continue_once can now consume an M56.3 authorization/preflight checkpoint and execute the existing Rust proposal.apply replace_file mutation boundary under objective, route, preflight, hash, and one-time authorization checks.

The Golden Journey can move from runtime-selected objective proposal review through controlled apply without a headless caller orchestrating separate proposal.apply calls or risking duplicate replay mutation.

The continuation checkpoint and bounded apply result provide a replay-safe agent-loop transition from explicit objective apply to progress inspection without exposing raw data or caller-side sequencing.

Rust validates journey/session/drive/task/run/proposal/source-event identity, candidate/context/path fingerprints, M56.3 authorization/preflight fingerprint, expected target hash, and latest apply preconditions before mutation.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances controlled_workspace_tools with direct support for headless_autonomous_development, persistent_structured_ledger, and runtime_permission_enforcement.
answers.new_capability: A headless caller can provide an objective_proposal_apply_target to headless.continue_once and have Rust apply exactly one approved replace_file objective proposal via the existing proposal.apply authority, returning a bounded apply result and replay checkpoint.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: proposal.apply alone is not bound to the Golden Journey candidate fingerprint, M56.3 authorization/preflight checkpoint, source route, objective/context fingerprints, or continuation replay identity.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: The Golden Journey would stop at an apply-ready route and still require caller-side apply orchestration before any actual workspace mutation can happen.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M56.1 context admission, M56.2 candidate binding, and M56.3 authorization/preflight because it performs the first objective-bound replace_file workspace mutation.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase extends existing headless.continue_once params and reuses proposal.apply internally; it adds no JSON-RPC method.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. It returns existing proposal_apply_result and a route; it adds no report, readiness, history, digest, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or summary endpoint.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust now validates the objective authorization/preflight checkpoint, delegates to proposal.apply for bounded replace_file mutation, records bounded continuation/apply evidence, and exact replay returns the same apply result without reapplying.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: The scheduled controller can advance from selected proposal review to a real workspace mutation and then progress inspection using one replay-safe continuation call.
answers.milestone_progress: This closes the first mutation boundary in M56 and enables later verification, recovery, and accepted-completion phases.

exit_criteria: headless.continue_once accepts a bounded objective_proposal_apply_target for apply_authorized_objective_proposal_explicitly routes
Rust validates M56.3 authorization/preflight checkpoint identity and fingerprint before applying
Rust validates journey/session/drive/task/run/proposal/source-event ids, operation/status labels, candidate/context/path fingerprints, expected snapshot/plan ids, and expected target SHA-256
The implementation delegates actual replace_file mutation to existing proposal.apply authority with authorize=true and request-only replacement_content
Success performs one atomic replace_file apply and returns existing proposal_apply_result with next_route.kind = inspect_progress_overview
Exact replay returns the same bounded proposal_apply_result without a second WorkspacePatchApplyResultRecorded event or second file mutation
Mismatch or stale authorization/preflight evidence fails before workspace mutation

Ledger/checkpoint/RPC payloads exclude raw prompts, provider responses, file content, diffs, stdout/stderr, commands, environment, raw requests, raw ledger payloads, absolute/canonical paths, secrets, and raw tokens
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test headless_continue_applies_objective_proposal_after_authorization_preflight_and_replays covers checkpoint-bound objective apply, denial-before-mutation, atomic replace_file, bounded result, checkpointing, and duplicate-free replay
Existing M56.3 tests continue to cover objective authorization/preflight route and mismatch denial before side effects
VSIX protocol tests accept bounded objective apply params and reject malformed or raw-data-bearing payloads

safety_boundary: requires explicit objective apply authorization and current M56.3 checkpoint evidence
stores replacement_content only as a request input and persists only its SHA-256/counts
non_goals: no shell, git, network, provider, service, verifier, scheduler, or daemon execution
rejected_alternatives: caller-side proposal.apply as the Golden Journey apply boundary
a new apply preview or readiness endpoint
persisting replacement content, raw request, file content, or diffs in continuation metadata
technical_debt: Verification after objective apply remains an explicit later phase.
Runtime lib.rs remains large and should be split only by a later behavior-preserving MOVE-only refactor.
next_capability_rationale: M56.5 should route from objective apply result to bounded verification/progress assessment, then recovery if verification fails.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M56.4 updates current and archived phase-value manifests for the objective-authorized replace_file apply route. Review must confirm guard enforcement is not weakened and no wrapper/report/readiness surface was added.
